newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-SCRAPPY WIN TAKES RANGERS CLOSER TO TITLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-SCRAPPY WIN TAKES RANGERS CLOSER TO TITLE.

text.p: Rangers moved significantly closer to their ninth successive Scottish league title on Sunday when they beat arch-rivals Celtic 1-0 in a virtual championship decider at Celtic Park.

The only goal of a scrappy game, marred by the second-half dismissals of Rangers striker Mark Hateley and Celtic defender Malky Mackay in seperate incidents, came a minute before halftime when Dane Brian Laudrup scored off a post after woeful defending.

Man of the match Laudrup, who scored the only goal when Rangers beat Celtic 1-0 at Celtic Park in November, got to the ball just before Mackay after Ian Durrant had lobbed goalkeeper Stewart Kerr, powerless to collect an under-hit backpass from Alan Stubbs.
"I always felt the first goal was going to be vital, and so it proved," said a disappointed Celtic manager Tommy Burns afterwards.
"But it was a very poor game as a spectacle. You had two sets of players terrified to make a mistake. It's a shame. The game should be about more than that."
Victory for Celtic would have moved them to within two points of Rangers, whose win took them eight points clear of Celtic at the top. Both sides have six more games to play.
Walter Smith, the Rangers manager, was magnanimous in victory, saying: "Of course we will not be claiming the title yet, though I might have a drink to celebrate the win tonight.
"We have now beaten Celtic four times this season but we're only eight points ahead. That shows our record against the other teams has not been as good as it could be. We cannot relax for a minute."

Rangers could also find themsleves in trouble with the Scottish Football Association for an incident after the game. The Rangers players mimicked Celtic's ritual pre-match huddle by performing their own victory huddle afterwards.
"I think they just did that for a laugh, there was nothing else in it," said Smith.
The huddle, though, followed some angry face-offs between the players after the final whistle, with Celtic's volatile Italian striker Paolo Di Canio in particular having to be restrained.
He appeared to be trying to single-handedly take on the entire Rangers' dugout before being guided towards the sanctuary of his own dressing room by two Celtic officials.
The match was full of intense rivalry but poor football, with crunching and ferocious tackling from both teams.
Celtic almost scored what would have been a memorable goal three minutes before halftime when Di Canio volleyed a 30-metre shot against the bar following a free kick.

The messy nature of the match was summed up by an unseemly skirmish midway through the second half which led to Hateley's dismissal, just 67 minutes into his return to Rangers after 18 months in London with Queens Park Rangers.
The 35-year-old English striker was shown the red card for appearing to head-butt Celtic keeper Stewart Kerr after Rangers had been awarded a free kick for an earlier infringment.
Celtic also finished the match with 10 men when Mackay was sent off in the 80th minute for hauling down Laudrup.

But Rangers, with six regular first team players missing through illness or injury, ended the game on a high note, moving within touching distance of equalling the record of nine sucessive titles achieved by Celtic between 1965 and 1974.
If they do that, goalkeeper Andy Dibble will have a great reason to remember what might prove to be his only match for Rangers.

The 31-year-old Manchester City third choice, signed as cover for Rangers because of the injury to first choice Andy Goram, found himself thrown into the match when No.2 keeper Theo Snelders was also injured.
He had a fine, if largely untroubled debut, making sure Rangers avenged their defeat to Celtic in the Scottish Cup last week.
